prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle;Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline. Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Business Rules Registry governs fairness/carriers/spacing/alert-subscriptions. Cedarbell normalizes intents against Airport Capacity Plan. Marlinstone estimates stand/apron/runway/departure-fix demand;Capacity Assessment Module compares Airport Acceptance Rate/runway-configuration/taxiway/sector-limits. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;runway/departure-fix/Ground Delay Program constraints;capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Copperfin authorizes Capacity Reduction State exceptions/recovery/divergence;receives departure-rate-erosion notifications;chooses metering/targeted-delay/rerouting/wider-regulation. Halcyon confirms publication,requests delay/fairness adjustments,checks resequencing/Slot Compliance State. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:advisory movements/timestamped milestones. Quartzline reconciles constraints,sends Stand Tow Request Form;Blueharbor recalculates. Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes capacity endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Lantern distributes approvals. Saffron shall confirm operator revisions before freeze-horizon;justified connection/crew/rotation reviews permitted;stable

New part:
S362: The Airline Operations Coordinator confirms whether each affected aircraft can absorb the assigned delay at stand without compromising crew, passenger, or turnaround constraints.
S363: If an operator cannot accept the proposed stand delay, the Aircraft Operator Representative requests reconsideration through the Airport CDM Portal.
S364: The Gate Conflict Detector warns when continued stand holding would block an inbound allocation or create a conflict with a planned equipment move.
S365: Business Rules Registry parameters define the maximum planned runway queue, the warning threshold, and the intervention threshold for each runway configuration.
S366: When a predicted queue exceeds the warning threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub highlights the affected runway queue on the Common Situation Display.
S367: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Regional Flow Manager may increase stand absorption to prevent unstable taxi queues from forming under reduced visibility or wet surface conditions.
S368: In a Capacity Reduction State, the Airport Duty Manager and Tower Supervisor agree whether the metering horizon should be extended so that delay is absorbed before pushback rather than near the runway.
S369: All changes to Target Off Block Time values, Calculated Takeoff Time values, and threshold overrides are written to the Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger.
S370: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares planned stand absorption, actual off block performance, and runway queue length to verify that the agreed thresholds were not exceeded.
S371: The Regional Flow Platform enters the winter operating mode when freezing precipitation, contamination reports, or low surface temperature forecasts make untreated ground movement unreliable.
S372: The Meteorology Briefing Officer confirms the trigger conditions in the Digital Briefing Room so that airport, airline, and tower participants share one operational assumption.
S373: In this mode, the Capacity Assessment Module reduces practical departure capacity to account for deicing time, pad transit time, and slower ramp taxi speeds.
S374: The Airport Capacity Plan is revised with a winter margin before the Slot Allocation Engine recalculates affected Calculated Takeoff Time values.
S375: The Deicing Coordinator maintains the active pad configuration, including open bays, closed bays, fluid limitations, and vehicle availability.
S376: Pad queue controls assign aircraft to a deicing lane only after the Target Off Block Time is stable enough to support a realistic treatment sequence.
S377: The Ramp Movement Board displays each aircraft as pending push, taxi to pad, in treatment, awaiting release, or returning to stand when treatment cannot be completed.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
